name: Harrowgate Industrial Plateau
description: A massive elevated industrial zone built atop the reinforced rooftops of a pre-Meridian heavy manufacturing district, Harrowgate is what happens when a city grows upward faster than it grows outward and someone decides the roofs of old factories make perfectly adequate foundations. The original buildings below — many still partially operational — form a dense substructure of crumbling brick, exposed rebar, and improvised reinforcement that occasionally shifts, sending minor tremors through the Plateau's floor. Above, a patchwork of active foundries, chemical processors, fabrication yards, and the warehouses of four mid-tier manufacturing corporations create a working industrial district that never fully sleeps.

sights: orange-lit foundry windows casting warm glow through perpetual smog
crane arms swinging loads overhead between buildings
steam venting from hundreds of pipes at irregular intervals
the constant orange haze of particulate matter backlit by work lights
corporate logos painted large on warehouse walls, faded and overlapping
workers in respirator masks moving in shift-change columns
sounds: rhythmic hammering and press-stamping from foundry floors
industrial fans cycling up and down
the grinding of heavy fabrication equipment
shift-change bells at irregular intervals across competing corporate schedules
structural groans from the substructure below
smells: the chemical sweetness of polymer processing
atmosphere.feel: Relentlessly functional and indifferent to human comfort — a place built to produce, not to house, where workers are components in a larger mechanism and the machinery's needs take priority over their own.

demographics: Predominantly shift-labor workforce living in company dormitory blocks, with a growing underclass of informal workers who live in the substructure below the Plateau floor. Significant population of augmented workers whose cybernetics were provided as employment terms — technically owned by the corporations that installed them. Supervisory and technical staff are largely Meridian-born, while floor labor draws from throughout the corridor.
economy: Heavy fabrication, metal processing, component manufacturing for the construction and infrastructure sectors, chemical synthesis, and corporate warehousing. Secondary economy in stolen materials, shift-labor brokering, and the informal markets that serve workers who can't leave during long contract periods.
power_structure: Four mid-tier manufacturing corporations — Vethane Industrial, Corsair Fabrication, Null-Grade Synthesis, and the locally-owned Harrow & Sons collective — maintain competing jurisdictions across the Plateau, each with private security forces whose territorial boundaries shift with contract wins and losses. A nominal Meridian industrial regulatory office exists here but has been effectively captured by Vethane's lobbying.
dangers: structural subsidence events when the substructure below shifts
industrial accidents with inadequate corporate response
corporate security forces detaining workers for 'contract violations'
air quality levels that exceed safe exposure limits during peak production
debt bondage through cybernetics ownership clauses in work contracts
chemical spills from Null-Grade Synthesis operations
sabotage between competing corporate factions endangering workers
opportunities: access to heavy fabrication equipment for off-book manufacturing
stolen industrial materials available at steep discounts
corporate espionage opportunities between competing manufacturers
the substructure below the Plateau contains entire abandoned factory floors
workers with specialized technical skills willing to freelance
Vethane Industrial's research division is working on something they've heavily classified
story_hooks: Three workers have disappeared during night shifts, and corporate security is actively suppressing the reports
A structural engineer has evidence that the Plateau's foundation is six months from a catastrophic failure and can't get anyone to listen
A worker whose corporate-owned cybernetics are being remotely throttled as punishment for union organizing needs help breaking the control signal
Something in the sealed substructure levels has started leaving marks on the underside of the Plateau floor — from below
Corsair Fabrication has begun quietly producing something that doesn't match any civilian manufacturing contract on record
frequented_by: Meridian regulatory officials on Vethane's payroll

notable_locations.name: The Drift Markets
notable_locations.description: An informal market that assembles in the gaps between corporate jurisdictions during the overlapping shift-change windows — roughly ninety minutes twice a day — when corporate security is occupied with personnel transitions. Food, contraband, gray-market augmentation services, and labor brokering happen in plain sight before dispersing.

notable_locations.name: Harrow & Sons Main Hall
notable_locations.description: The oldest standing structure on the Plateau, a massive pre-Meridian foundry still operated by the Harrow family collective — one of the last worker-owned operations in the district. Its workforce is fiercely protective of their independence, and the building itself serves as a de facto community center and refuge for workers in trouble with the corporate operators.

notable_locations.name: The Underbelly Access
notable_locations.description: A series of maintenance hatches in the Plateau floor, theoretically secured by corporate lock systems, that lead down into the abandoned factory substructure. The locks have been compromised for years. Below is a city within a city — entire production floors frozen in mid-operation, machinery still in place, and a population of informal residents who have never appeared on any census.
